::: {.callout-warning title="Static schema evidence"}
This page describes exported VBA at
`3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435`. It does not certify the schema of
an existing deployment, supported database versions, migrations, transaction
behaviour, backup integrity, or production configuration.
:::

## Database roles and types

`clsDB` represents a database connection and cached domain collections. Global
state distinguishes a base database, a temporary exchange database, and an
optional satellite database.

The `DBTypes` enum defines:

| Value | Identifier | Source status |
|---:|---|---|
| 0 | `nodb` | No active database. |
| 1 | `Sqlexpress` | SQL Server-style connection using `SQLOLEDB`. The identifier does not prove an Express-only requirement. |
| 2 | `mdb` | Retained for old registry values and explicitly unsupported by the open workflow. |
| 3 | `accdb` | Microsoft Access file through the configured ACE OLE DB provider. |

SQL connections use integrated Windows security when `DBUser` is empty;
otherwise the source builds a connection string with supplied user name and
password. Access uses `Microsoft.ACE.OLEDB.<configured version>` and the database
file path. Driver availability, Office bitness, TLS, SQL Server support, and
least-privilege configuration are **environment-dependent**.

## Registry configuration

`InterfaceRegistry` uses VBA `GetSetting`, `SaveSetting`, and `DeleteSetting`.
On Windows these settings are below:

`HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\VB and VBA Program Settings\NADABAS`

| Section | Values observed in source |
|---|---|
| `Language` | `Code` |
| `ACEOLEDB` | `Version` |
| `Database` and numbered `Database1` ... | `Number`, `DBType`, `Source`, `Catalog`, `User`, `PW`, `DBName` |
| `Satellite` and numbered satellite sections | `Number`, `DBName`, `LinkedTo` |
| `ExchDB` | `DBName`, `DBType` |
| `Document` | Last path used by the document picker. |

::: {.callout-important title="Credentials are a security finding"}
The source can persist a database password in registry value `PW`. Recording
this fact does not approve the design. Do not publish actual values. Determine
whether affected deployments use password authentication, assess registry
protection and logging exposure, and track migration to an approved credential
mechanism.
:::

## Opening and initializing

`cmdOpen_Close_Database` selects a configured database, builds a connection
string, creates `ADODB.Connection` and `ADOX.Catalog` objects, and tests whether
the database has required NADABAS tables.

For a base database, `TestDbOK` requires `KeyNames`, `Administrators`, and
`Workbooks`. An exchange database requires `KeyNames`; a satellite requires
`Workbooks`. If required structures are absent, the user may be offered
initialization. `InitializeDB` creates `KeyNames`, `Administrators`, and
`Workbooks`, then establishes Access base-path and user settings where
applicable. This confirms the retained draft's three initial base tables, but
only as source behaviour; it does not prove every deployed database began that
way.

After the required tables have been found or initialized, NADABAS runs an
idempotent workbook-identity migration. The migration creates the identity
catalog, adds numeric workbook-reference columns, backfills them from existing
names, widens compatibility name columns, and rebuilds affected unique indexes.
It records `WorkbookIdentityV1` in `NADABASSchemaMigrations` only after all steps
succeed. The same check runs during Access/SQL conversion, where existing IDs are
preserved.

## Shared ADO routines

[`DBInterface.bas`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/DBInterface.bas)
owns module-level recordsets and exposes cursor-style routines.

| Routine group | Source behaviour |
|---|---|
| `DbExecute` | Execute SQL through `CurrentDB.DBCnn`, log it when SQL logging is active, and return affected-row count. |
| `CreateCursor` | Open an update-capable recordset using engine-specific cursor and lock modes. |
| `CreateSnapshot` | Open a static, read-only recordset. |
| `CreateGetCursor`, `CreateSumCursor` | Open additional recordsets used for copy and aggregation paths. |
| `Cursor...`, `GetColumn...`, `PutColumn...` | Navigate, read, insert, update, delete, and count cursor operations. |
| `Close...Cursor` | Close recordsets; `CloseCursor` calls `UpdateBatch` before closing when open. |

`DbFunc.OpenDb` and `CloseDB` maintain a nesting counter and Excel wait cursor;
they do not open and close the `ADODB.Connection` on every call. When the count
reaches zero, `doclose` closes module recordsets only for Access and restores the
Excel cursor. The retained draft's simpler “open/close database” description is
therefore not an accurate connection-lifecycle contract.

String-building helpers include `InQ`, `InB`, `InBTF`, and `NowFunction`.
`InQ` escapes embedded apostrophes and surrounds text with a SQL string literal.
Much of the application still builds SQL by concatenating strings. Treat full
parameterization and injection resistance as unresolved security work,
especially for workbook-, form-, file-, and registry-derived values.

## Source-defined system tables

[`DbCreateTables.bas`](https://github.com/statisticsnorway/nadabas/blob/3b4c05386e5a44d05633136ecbcf5dd067f70435/vba/modules/DbCreateTables.bas)
defines the following structures. “Unique index” means the creation routine
builds one; it is not proof that an existing deployment has it.

| Table | Columns created by source | Source-defined uniqueness or role |
|---|---|---|
| `Administrators` | `UserName` | Unique index on `UserName`; administrator identity list. |
| `BasePath` | `BasePath` | Single-path convention enforced by application logic. |
| `BackupPath` | `BackupPath` | Backup folder/template path. |
| `BatchList` | `Listname`, `ItemNo`, `WorkbookID`, `Workbookname` | Unique index on list and item order; the name is retained for compatibility/display. |
| `BatchDescription` | `Listname`, `Description` | Unique index on list name. |
| `Batch2List` | `Listname`, `ItemNo`, `Batchname` | Ordered list of batch names; unique index on list and item. |
| `Batch2Description` | `Listname`, `Description` | Unique index on list name. |
| `Classifications` | `ClassName`, `Code`, `Title` | Unique index on class and code. |
| `ClassificationDescriptions` | `ClassName`, `Description` | Unique index on class name. This table was omitted from the retained table inventory. |
| `Correspondences` | `Fromclass`, `FromCode`, `Toclass`, `ToCode` | Maps source classification codes to target codes; unique index is created on the first three columns. |
| `DataLinks` | `KeyFamily`, `TargetWorkbookID`, `TargetWB`, `TargetDataArea`, `SourceWorkbookID`, `SourceWB`, `SourceDataArea` | Unique index uses key family, both numeric workbook IDs, and both data-area names. |
| `Descriptions` | `WorkbookID`, `WorkbookName`, `DataAreaName`, `TableName`, `GetPut`, `Description` | Unique index on numeric workbook ID and data-area name. |
| `DescriptionDimensions` | `WorkbookID`, `WorkbookName`, `DataAreaName`, `DimensionNumber`, `DimensionName`, `Classification`, `ConstantValue` | Unique index on numeric workbook ID, data area, and dimension order. |
| `DimensionClass` | `DimensionName`, `ClassName` | Default dimension-to-classification association; no index is created here. |
| `DBGlobals` | `IDNum`, `Name`, `Value` | Unique index on ordering identifier. |
| `Documents` | `Name`, `Path`, `Level`, `DGroup`, `WorkbookID`, `Workbook` | Global, group, or workbook document metadata; the ID is nullable for non-workbook documents. |
| `KeyNames` | `KeyName` | Unique index; identifies user-defined key-family tables. |
| `NADABASVersion` | `VersionNumber` | Version compatibility marker. |
| `NADABASSchemaMigrations` | `MigrationName`, `AppliedAt` | Records completed, idempotent schema migrations. |
| `Permissions` | `WorkbookID`, `WorkBookName`, `User` | Workbook/user permission rows; no index is created here. |
| `UserSettings` | Colour, font, password, workbook/document policy, load/save, Dropbox, satellite, and import/export fields | One settings row is assumed by application code; no index is created here. |
| `WorkbookIdentities` | `WorkbookID`, `WorkbookName` | Generated numeric identity with unique indexes on both ID and current name. |
| `Workbooks` | `WorkbookID`, `WorkBookName`, `Title`, `GroupName`, `Path`, `ReservedBy`, `Status`, `ReservedDate`, `isdirty`, `LastGet`, `LastPut`, `Updateorder` | Unique indexes on numeric ID and workbook name. |
| `Year` | `Name`, `StartYear`, `EndYear`, `DefaultFormat` | Period-selection settings; no index is created here. |

Numeric workbook IDs are the relational keys used by current read, write,
rename, reporting, and source-link paths. Compatibility name columns remain so
older reports and integrations continue to work, and are synchronized during a
rename. These name columns are defined as text up to 255 characters; they are no
longer part of the wide composite `DataLinks` index.

The source does not create explicit foreign-key relationships in these routines.
It does create unique indexes, so the retained draft statement “there are no
constraints” is too broad. Whether a deployed database has additional primary
keys, foreign keys, checks, defaults, triggers, or manually added constraints is
**unknown** until its schema is inspected.

## Key-family data tables

`CreateNewKeyFam` creates one table named after each key family. For every
dimension it adds a non-null text column, then adds:

| Column | Source-defined type or role |
|---|---|
| `Value` | Single, double, or text, selected when the key family is created. |
| `Comment` | Long text. |
| `Formula` | Text column retained in the schema; current usage needs runtime and call-site review. |
| `Username` | User recorded for a write. |
| `ExcelFile` | Workbook provenance, normally without path/extension in application logic. |
| `Timestamp` | Write time. |
| `DataArea` | Workbook named-range provenance. |

A unique index is created across all dimension columns. The workbook/data-area
provenance fields are used by conflict, ownership, cleanup, and source-tracking
flows. They are not a substitute for a documented audit, retention, or
transaction model.

### Access-to-SQL conversion

During Access-to-SQL conversion, `cmdConvertDB` identifies key-family
dimensions by schema position: every field before `Value` is a dimension. A
name such as `Status`, `Changed`, or `Locked` is therefore valid for a
dimension and is not treated as metadata merely because of its name.

Before copying the first row of any table, the converter verifies that the SQL
target contains every source column. A mismatch reports the table and missing
columns and stops that table before rows are copied. Column assignment errors
are propagated to the conversion error handler instead of being reduced to a
message that allows conversion to continue. A failed conversion may still
leave tables copied earlier in the target database; discard or recreate that
target before retrying. The Access source is not changed by the copy workflow.

## Schema and SQL review priorities

1. Export schemas from representative non-production Access and SQL Server
   databases and compare them with `DbCreateTables`.
2. Record supported database, provider, Office-bitness, and authentication
   combinations.
3. Identify all string-concatenated SQL inputs and migrate high-risk paths to
   parameterized commands.
4. Define transaction boundaries for multi-table rename/delete, load/save,
   conversion, and administrative operations.
5. Specify concurrency, ownership conflict, retry, rollback, and reconciliation
   behaviour.
6. Verify backup and restore with recovery tests; do not infer recoverability
   from successful file-copy messages.
